newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA'S BATSMEN STRUGGLE IN FIRST SESSION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA'S BATSMEN STRUGGLE IN FIRST SESSION.

text.p: Australia's batsmen struggled against India's bowling attack on a dry and cracking wicket on the opening day of the one-off test at New Delhi's Feroze Shah Kotla stadium on Thursday.
Opting to bat first, Australia were 81 for two at lunch with opener Michael Slater unbeaten on 34.
Skipper Mark Taylor and Ricky Ponting were the batsmen out in the first session.

Medium pacer Venkatesh Prasad beat Taylor twice in one over before finally trapping him lbw for 27 after he offered no stroke. Taylor batted for 72 minutes, faced 51 deliveries and struck four boundaries.
Ponting (14) was yorked by off-spinner Aashish Kapoor as he shaped for an off-drive in the over before lunch.
Slater, who looked the most confident of Australia's batsmen, had struck four boundaries during his two-hour stay at the wicket.
